s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea and joint pain in a patient with a history of rheumatic mitral stenosis and recent valve procedures
salient_findings: Progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and positive C-reactive protein
key_facts: 36-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis
Status post mitral valvotomy and two valve repairs
Received streptokinase for suspected prosthetic mitral valve thrombosis two weeks earlier
Experienced fever and bilateral knee pain over the past 3 days
No photosensitivity, rashes, myalgia, malaise, or lymphadenopathy
Hemoglobin 9.65 g/dL, neutrophils 41%, lymphocytes 43%, platelets 4,456,000/µL
Prothrombin time 32.8 s, INR 2.5
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and positive C-reactive protein
Blood and urine cultures were sterile
Serologic tests for hepatitis B surface antigen, antinuclear antibody, anti–cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and lactate dehydrogenase were negative

shortlist.why_kept: Recent streptokinase administration and symptoms of fever and joint pain

shortlist.label: Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: History of valve procedures and recent symptoms of fever

shortlist.why_kept: History of valve procedures and recent symptoms of fever

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of fever, bilateral knee pain, and elevated inflammatory markers, combined with the recent administration of streptokinase, are consistent with serum sickness, a known adverse reaction to certain medications, including streptokinase.

rejected.label: Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
rejected.why: Blood and urine cultures were sterile, making infective endocarditis less likely

rejected.label: Acute Rheumatic Fever
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of typical symptoms such as migratory polyarthritis and carditis make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Dressler Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of cardiac surgery, the timing and symptoms do not align with Dressler Syndrome, which typically occurs weeks to months after surgery

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: The sterile blood and urine cultures, along with the lack of other signs of infection, make this diagnosis unlikely
